newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed barely changed after comments by a Bundesbank official sparked a sell-off in Bund futures.
Guilder bond prices, which had been showing healthy gains to that stage, were marked down in response to the dive although dealers said they saw little client selling.

Dealers said Bund futures dropped sharply on news that Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse told a German newspaper that the Maastricht Treaty would have to be renegotiated if European economic and monetary union (EMU) was delayed.
"It was a real sell-off," said one dealer.
He said it prompted a return to switching out of guilder state loans into German Bunds, especially in the 30-year sector.
But another dealer saw no reason to panic as a result of the 11th hour events. "It was future's driven after the comment. There was nothing happening in cash," he said.
The yield on the 10-year benchmark, the February 2007 bond, ended at 5.45 percent, down from 5.46 percent the previous day, but the January 2023 yield edged up to 6.16 percent from 6.12.
Dutch paper had looked set to finish higher for the second successive day after quiet range-bound trading in which sellers were thin on the ground.
"We are stuck in a trading range at the moment," said one trader.
Before the sell-off, a broker said she had seen switching out of the new February 2007 bond into November 2006 and January 2006 paper.
But one dealer said he found few sellers of middle-curve paper. "It was difficult to get an offer," he said.
The Dutch yield curve had steepened in early trading but flattened again through the day.
